transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess… it’s a little embarrassing, but I’ve been noticing I can’t seem to stay seated when I’m supposed to. Like during client interviews, or tutoring sessions, even book club—I’ll keep getting up, finding some reason to move around. I don’t mean to be disruptive, and I’m still listening, mostly, but people are starting to notice that I can’t just sit and listen.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized or high, like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m busy or kind of keyed up, but not “high” exactly, and I don’t think I’ve ever felt like I didn’t need sleep. If anything, I still notice when I haven’t gotten enough. Is that what you mean?
When you were a child, did you also have trouble staying seated in class or other situations where you were expected to sit still?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I did fine academically, so I guess it didn’t look like I was trying to cause trouble, but my grade-school report cards always had some version of “bright, but can’t stay in her seat” or “needs to wait her turn.” My mother still teases me that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I needed to pace through. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often find your mind drifting or getting easily distracted when you’re supposed to focus on something?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, everyone’s mind wanders sometimes, right? I don’t want to overstate it. I haven’t really noticed that as the main problem, but maybe I’d need you to say more about what you mean by “distracted.”
When you have to stay seated, do you feel anxious?

I don’t know that I’d call it anxious, exactly. Maybe a little… restless or uncomfortable, but not like I’m scared or panicking. I just start feeling like I should be doing something, if that makes sense. But I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by anxious.
When you try to stay seated, do you feel a strong inner urge to get up and move?

Yes… I think “urge” is probably the right word. I try to sit still and listen, but after a while it’s like my body is already looking for a reason to get up. I’ll stand to check something, refill water, move papers—anything that makes it seem purposeful.

It’s actually part of why I’m here. It’s been happening in client interviews, when I’m tutoring, even at book club, and people are starting to notice that I can’t just sit and listen. I don’t mean to be rude. It just feels really hard to stay put.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your attention drifts?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I do finish things most of the time, especially if they matter or someone’s waiting on them. I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m just drifting off and abandoning tasks all day.

Maybe I’d need to think about it more, but attention drifting doesn’t feel like the main reason I have trouble. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do people often tell you that you talk more than they expect, or that it’s hard to get a word in when you get going?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try not to be someone who dominates a conversation, but I have been told I can kind of… keep going.

Especially with work, if I’m talking through a case or a client meeting, I’ll go through every angle out loud, and then I realize I’ve basically taken up all the space. Sometimes the other person is giving me signs they’re done—checking the time, shorter answers—and I still find myself finishing the whole thought. I don’t mean to be inconsiderate. I just get going and it’s hard to stop at the right point.
Do you often interrupt other people before they’ve finished speaking?

Sometimes, yes. I don’t love admitting that, because I don’t want to sound like I’m rude or trying to take over.

At work, if I hear junior detectives talking through a lead, I’ll jump in with questions or suggestions before anyone has actually asked me. And even outside work, like if a neighbor is talking in the hallway, I might sort of insert myself with advice or a question. In the moment it feels helpful, but afterward I’ll think, “Oh… that wasn’t really my conversation to enter.”

So yes, I guess I do interrupt or intrude at times. I try to mean it well, but I can see how it comes across.
Do you often feel excessive worry, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

I don’t think so… not excessive worry, no. I mean, I worry about normal things—work going smoothly, whether I handled something the right way—but it usually has a reason behind it.

I wouldn’t say I’m just anxious for no clear reason most of the time. At least, I haven’t noticed that being a big issue. Does that make sense?
Have you often been spiteful or tried to get back at people?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I can get irritated with people, sure, especially if I feel like someone’s being careless or wasting time, but I don’t think I’m someone who tries to punish people or get revenge.

If I’ve ever been sharp with someone, it’s usually more in the moment, not like I’m sitting there planning to get back at them. I hope that makes sense.
Do you often have a hard time waiting your turn?

I’m not sure I’d say “often”… but I do notice I get impatient, yes.

Like if I’m waiting in line or someone is taking a long time to make a decision, I can feel myself wanting to jump ahead or move things along. I usually try not to make it obvious, because I know that’s not fair to other people. But inside, yes, waiting my turn can feel harder than I’d like to admit.

Does that answer what you mean?
Do you often feel “on the go,” as if you’re driven by a motor?

Yes… I think that one probably does fit, though I don’t love how it sounds.

Even on days when I don’t have field work, I don’t really just relax. I’ll go from unpacking boxes to reorganizing case files to running errands, almost like I’m still chasing a lead or something. It feels like I should be doing something.

I can be “off duty” technically, but I have a hard time actually being off, if that makes sense.
